findings.title: A lone failure of the post-removal recount is treated identically to “removeCurrency itself may have failed”, discarding a fully-confirmed item count and aborting a purchase that removeCurrency actually completed
findings.scenario: buy(player, 40) with 64 plain iron ingots in inventory and a healthy pool (bonus=500). removeCurrency(inventory, 40) runs to completion with NO exception (it physically removes exactly 40, leaving 24 — verified empirically, see below). Immediately after, the verification-only call `itemsTaken = beforeTake - countCurrency(inventory)` (line 291) throws (e.g. an Error surfaces while re-reading getStorageContents() under transient heap pressure — a call that happens strictly after removeCurrency returned, so it cannot itself be evidence that removeCurrency's own mutation was incomplete). The catch at lines 293-299 sets itemsTaken = UNKNOWN and failure = thrown regardless of whether removeCurrency threw. Because blocksMutated is then false (B10/B11 never runs) and itemsTaken == UNKNOWN, refundSkipped becomes true at line 403, so U2 never calls deliver() and the purchase throws IllegalStateException with ZERO items refunded and ZERO blocks granted. I reproduced this against the real working-tree class with the harness's own PlayerInventory stub (its `throwOnGetStorageContentsCallN` knob, which fails only the Nth getStorageContents() call and leaves setStorageContents/removeCurrency itself untouched): after the call, sumPlainCurrency(c) == 24 (i.e. removeCurrency genuinely took all 40, exactly as requested), c.data.setterArguments is empty (no grant attempted), and the SEVERE log reads '...an unknown number taken, 0 returned (the refund was deliberately skipped)... Fix by hand: Inspect the inventory: up to 40 iron ingots may be missing and were not refunded automatically.' The player is left having lost exactly 40 items for certain, received nothing for them, and the operator is handed a hedged 'up to 40 may be missing' instead of a precise 'give back 40' — even though the only source of uncertainty was a diagnostic re-read that runs strictly after the mutation, not the mutation itself. final_spec.json's B9 sub-case explicitly scopes this UNKNOWN/skip-refund treatment to 'removeCurrency threw AND the recount also threw'; the code applies it whenever the recount alone throws, which is a materially different (and here, empirically confirmed avoidable) precondition not covered by that numbered step or by the residual_risks list.
findings.harness_gap: None of BUY-TAKE-THROWS-AND-RECOUNT-THROWS or any other injection isolates a recount failure from a removeCurrency failure; the only recount-throws test (injBuyTakeThrowsAndRecountThrows) forces BOTH throwInSetStorageContentsAfterSlotK and alsoFailNextReadAfterSetStorageContentsThrow together, so it can only ever exercise the compound case. The stub already exposes `throwOnGetStorageContentsCallN`, which is exactly the tool needed for the isolated case (I used it: setup(mirror,500,100) + putCurrency(c,0,64) + `c.inv.throwOnGetStorageContentsCallN = 4` + buy(c.player, 40)) but no injection uses it that way. A missing assertion in that new injection should check that when removeCurrency itself produced no CallLog entry indicating a throw, the eventual state is NOT itemsTaken==UNKNOWN with a full skipped refund but instead a confident, measured itemsTaken.
findings.fix_hint: Don't let a failure of the verification read alone erase what is already known: if the removeCurrency try (lines 279-286) completed without recording a failure, the amount actually removed is bounded by `items` by removeCurrency's own loop invariant (remaining only decreases, starting at items) and, absent a foreign inventory writer (already treated as unreachable elsewhere in this file's own reasoning), is exactly `items`. Mirror the fallback pattern already used in deliver() for its own before-count failure (a degraded-but-non-UNKNOWN estimate) instead of collapsing straight to the UNKNOWN sentinel whenever ONLY the post-removal recount throws while removeCurrency itself signaled success.

findings.title: deliver() is battle-tested against listener interference only via sell()'s payout call; buy()'s refund call to the same method has no equivalent regression coverage
findings.scenario: Every adverse-listener injection (cancelled ItemSpawnEvent, shrinking/merging drop, teleport, kick, drop-throws-unconfirmed, addItem-throws-after-partial) is wired up only against sell()'s deliver(...) call (SELL-PAYOUT-*). No BUY-side injection ever gives the refund path (line 410, `deliver(player, itemsTaken, "refund for a failed purchase", refund);`) a full-inventory or listener-interfering setup. I built and ran an equivalent scenario against the real class myself (buy(player,64) with 64 held, store.savePlayerData throwing OutOfMemoryError to force the unwind, c.inv.freeSlotOverride=0 to force the whole refund to the ground, and c.world.shrinkDropNumberTo.put(1,1) to shrink the dropped stack): the shared deliver() code handled it correctly — pool restored to 500, refund correctly measured as 1 of 64 delivered, both the 'Give back 63 iron ingots...' and the mandatory 'Verify the player's file... bonus=6900... /adjustbonusclaimblocks Steve -6400' clauses fired together as designed, and the original OutOfMemoryError was rethrown. So this is currently correct, not a live bug — but it is unprotected: any future change that alters how buy() constructs its Handover, computes itemsTaken, or wires the try/catch around its deliver() call (distinct code from sell()'s call site) could silently break the buy-side refund's accounting or its compositional fix-by-hand clauses without any of the 54 existing injections noticing, since none of them drive buy()'s refund through anything but a wide-open inventory.

missing_injections: No injection ever produces `invalid-amount` (buy with items<=0 or sell with blocks<=0 is never called), even though this is one of the 14 keys the NO-INVENTED-KEYS injection claims to cover.
No injection ever produces `limit-reached`, even though `setup()`'s `maxPurchasedBlocks` parameter exists specifically to drive it (every call site that passes it explicitly passes 0 = disabled).
No injection ever produces `not-enough-blocks` (sell() with purchased < blocks) — sell()'s first refusal guard is never exercised.

No injection ever produces `blocks-in-use` (sell() with available=getRemainingClaimBlocks() < blocks) — this also means the design's own documented GriefPrevention behaviour ('maps arithmetic overflow to 0, which reads here as blocks-in-use') is never exercised despite PlayerData.remainingOverride existing precisely to model it (remainingOverride is set exactly once across the whole suite, in SELL-HAPPY, to a value equal to purchased).

vacuous_assertions.where: driver/Harness.java: checkSetterNeverThrew(Ctx) (called from every one of the 27 injections) is the sole implementation of harness_plan.json's invariant #5, 'PRE-BOXED SETTER'.
vacuous_assertions.why_vacuous: The plan states this invariant checks 'the setter call log must show that every argument was an Integer object created before the first mutation of that trade (identity comparison against the PREPARE boxes) or, on the relative-correction branch only, a fresh box created in a guarded step.' The implementation only asserts `!c.data.setterThrowsFired`, and PlayerData.setterThrows only fires when `setBonusClaimBlocks` is called with a literal null argument (stubs/me/ryanhamshire/GriefPrevention/PlayerData.java, setBonusClaimBlocks). decisions.id: FINDING-1: lone post-removal recount failure collapses to UNKNOWN and skips the refund
decisions.semantics: buy(): removeCurrency returns normally, then the B9 verification recount (countCurrency -> getStorageContents) throws. itemsTaken becomes UNKNOWN, failure is the recount's throwable, no grant is made, the refund is skipped, the SEVERE says 'an unknown number taken, 0 returned (the refund was deliberately skipped) ... Inspect the inventory: up to N ... may be missing', and U7 rethrows.
decisions.reasoning: Rejected as a code finding: the code does exactly what the spec says, and the scenario is an accepted residual risk. final_spec.json step B9 prescribes the recount as its own `try { itemsTaken = beforeTake - countCurrency(inventory); } catch (Throwable thrown) { itemsTaken = UNKNOWN; if (failure == null) failure = thrown; }`. The `if (failure == null)` branch only does anything when removeCurrency did NOT throw. So the numbered step already covers the lone-recount case and says UNKNOWN for it. BarterService.java lines 289-300 copy it word for word, and line 403 is U2's `refundSkipped = (blocksMutated && !poolRestored) || itemsTaken == UNKNOWN` word for word. The failure_table row the finding quotes ('removeCurrency threw AND the recount also threw') describes the compound case. It never says 'only', and it does not narrow B9. The recount can throw only an Error from getStorageContents or its array allocation, i.e. heap exhaustion. residual_risks already accepts that: 'Under genuine heap exhaustion ... the refund, the recounts ... may all fail ... the operator record is best-effort'. I reproduced it in a scratch copy of the harness (throwOnGetStorageContentsCallN=4, which is the B9 recount: calls 1-3 are the B2 count, the PREPARE beforeTake and removeCurrency's read). Under both semantics 24 of 64 remain, setterArguments is empty and the SEVERE matches. One correction to the finding: the stub throws java.lang.Error, so U7 rethrows that Error, not IllegalStateException. The record is truthful: 'up to 40' covers exactly 40. The finding's fix, taking itemsTaken = items on a normal removeCurrency return, would trust instead of measure. That goes against B9 ('the measurement must survive...'), against the javadoc claim 'No number is reported ... that the plugin did not measure', and against the class javadoc at lines 168-171, so it is a spec change for a human to decide, not a code fix.

No injection separates a recount failure from a removeCurrency failure. BUY-TAKE-THROWS-AND-RECOUNT-THROWS always sets both throwInSetStorageContentsAfterSlotK and alsoFailNextReadAfterSetStorageContentsThrow. So the `if (failure == null) failure = thrown` branch of B9, the only branch that runs when removeCurrency completes, is never executed. A regression there would pass silently, for example refunding a guess, attaching the wrong throwable, or granting after an unmeasured take. The finding suggests asserting that the state is NOT UNKNOWN; that contradicts spec B9 and must not be adopted. The injection has to pin B9 as written.

spec_gaps_for_human: final_spec B9 vs failure_table: step B9's recount catch (`itemsTaken = UNKNOWN; if (failure == null) failure = thrown;`) prescribes an unknown count and a skipped refund even when removeCurrency returned normally and only the verification recount threw. The failure_table has a row only for the compound case, 'removeCurrency threw AND the recount also threw'. The code follows B9 word for word. Decide whether the lone-recount case should (a) keep UNKNOWN: a bounded, logged possible loss, as implemented now; or (b) trust removeCurrency's normal return as itemsTaken = items, stated as unmeasured in the SEVERE, and refund. Option (b) risks duplication only if a foreign inventory writer runs between PREPARE and the take, which the spec elsewhere calls unreachable on one thread, but it breaks the 'measured, never trusted' rule in B9 and the javadoc. Either way, add a failure_table row for this case. The new BUY-RECOUNT-ALONE-THROWS injection pins (a) until you decide.

harness_plan invariant #5 (PRE-BOXED SETTER) asks for an 'identity comparison against the PREPARE boxes'. A black-box harness cannot do that: PlayerData.getBonusClaimBlocks returns a primitive int, and no PREPARE-created Integer ever reaches a stub before the undo. findings.title: Recount-alone-throws after a clean take is treated as total unrefundable loss
findings.scenario: Player holds >= N plain currency items. buy(player, N) runs: removeCurrency(inventory, N) (line 281) completes WITHOUT throwing, and by construction of removeCurrency's own loop (which only stops once `remaining` reaches 0, already validated held>=N moments earlier on the single Bukkit main thread) this deterministically means exactly N items left the inventory. Immediately after, the sole confirmatory read on line 291 (`itemsTaken = beforeTake - countCurrency(inventory)`) throws on its own (e.g. a transient allocation failure inside getStorageContents, unrelated to removeCurrency). The catch at line 293-299 sets itemsTaken = UNKNOWN and failure = thrown. Because itemsTaken == UNKNOWN, refundSkipped is forced true at line 403, so U2 never calls deliver() — none of the N items are refunded — and because blocksMutated is still false, no blocks are granted either. The Error is rethrown (line 513) so the player sees only the generic dispatcher error. The player has permanently lost all N items for literally nothing, while the operator SEVERE at line 496-502 reports 'an unknown number taken ... up to N ... may be missing and were not refunded automatically' — language that describes genuine uncertainty, when in fact the plugin already possesses a 100%-certain count (N) it chose not to use.

findings.title: Double-precision price formula silently shorts the player by one item for ordinary non-power-of-two refund ratios
findings.scenario: With an entirely ordinary admin config such as `refund-ratio: 0.7`, `blocks-per-item: 1`, selling exactly 90 claim blocks computes `items = (int) Math.floor(blocks / (double) settings.blocksPerItem() * settings.refundRatio())` = floor(90 * 0.7). Because 0.7 has no exact binary floating-point representation, the double product evaluates to 62.999999999999993 rather than 63.0, so items comes out 62 instead of the mathematically exact 63 — verified numerically (Python Decimal/Fraction cross-check: mismatch reproduces at blocks=90,170,180,330,340,350,360,650,...,1460 for ratio 0.7, and similarly for e.g. 0.29, 0.9 at other block counts). The player is quietly paid one fewer item than the configured ratio promises, with no log line, no WARNING, and a plain 'sold' success message — deliver() truthfully places/drops exactly the `items` it was asked for, but the upstream price computation itself already shorted the player before delivery even started.
findings.harness_gap: Every sell-path injection in Harness.java sets refundRatio to either 1.0 (all the payout/listener-interference tests) or the untouched default 0.5 (the two purchase-ceiling tests at driver lines 1616/1636) — both exactly representable in binary — so no assertion anywhere compares the computed `items` against the mathematically exact decimal conversion for a fractional, non-power-of-two ratio (0.7, 0.9, 0.3, 0.6, ...), which is exactly the kind of value an operator is expected to configure; config.yml's own shipped default of 0.5 happens to dodge the very bug no test exercises.
findings.fix_hint: Compute the sale price with exact arithmetic instead of a double multiply-then-floor — e.g. represent refundRatio as a validated rational (numerator/denominator) at BarterSettings construction time and do `Math.floorDiv(blocks * numerator, blocksPerItem * denominator)`, or use BigDecimal with an explicit FLOOR rounding mode — so the result matches the configured ratio exactly instead of depending on binary floating-point representability.

findings.title: sell() javadoc overstates getRemainingClaimBlocks() overflow direction as always safe
findings.scenario: An operator (or GriefPrevention itself, whose own /adjustbonusclaimblocks has no upper bound) sets a player's bonus pool to a value close to Integer.MAX_VALUE, and the player also has non-trivial accrued and/or permission-group bonus blocks, such that accrued+bonus+groupBonus overflows int range inside PlayerData.getRemainingClaimBlocks(). javap of PlayerData.class shows two separate try/catch(ArithmeticException) ranges in that method: the SUM stage (accrued+bonus, then +groupBonus, both via Math.addExact) is caught and clamped to Integer.MAX_VALUE, after which the claim-area subtraction loop runs from that ceiling and returns a large positive number close to Integer.MAX_VALUE, not 0; only a SECOND overflow, inside the claim-area subtractExact loop itself, returns 0. Because sell()'s S6 guard is `if (available < blocks) return fail("blocks-in-use")` (line 577-581), a sum-stage overflow makes `available` enormous, so the guard never fires for any realistic `blocks` argument -- exactly the opposite of the class's own claim at line 539 that overflow 'reads here as blocks-in-use - the safe direction.' The sale then proceeds even though it should have been refused as committed-to-claims. Note the spec's own residual_risks entry #9 already hedges correctly ('maps arithmetic overflow to Integer.MAX_VALUE or 0 internally'), but the numbered step S6 in final_spec.json drops that nuance to a bare 'maps arithmetic overflow to 0', and BarterService.java's sell() javadoc reproduces that narrower, bytecode-contradicted version verbatim.
findings.harness_gap: The harness's PlayerData stub only exposes getRemainingClaimBlocks() via a hand-set `remainingOverride` field (stubs/me/ryanhamshire/GriefPrevention/PlayerData.java); it never models GriefPrevention's real addExact/subtractExact overflow arithmetic, so no injection drives the actual sum-overflow-vs-subtraction-overflow branches, and no assertion compares the shipped javadoc's overflow claim against the decompiled jar. A SELL-BLOCKS-IN-USE-SUM-OVERFLOW scenario setting remainingOverride to a value derived from the verified addExact-then-clamp-to-MAX_VALUE behavior (rather than 0) would have caught the mismatch.
findings.fix_hint: Either correct the comment to state the asymmetric truth verified via javap -- sum-stage overflow clamps toward Integer.MAX_VALUE (favoring the sale, not refusal), and only the claim-area subtraction stage can yield 0 -- or drop the specific-value claim entirely and say GriefPrevention's own overflow behavior here is unspecified/not relied upon for safety, matching the more careful wording already used in the design's own residual-risk notes.

findings.title: info() javadoc overclaims exclusivity of the fix-negative WARNING
findings.scenario: warmClaimData() (lines 854-865) is the single helper called identically from buy() (line 212), sell() (line 571) and info() (line 831), and it emits the exact same WARNING ('GriefPrevention corrected <player>'s bonus pool from X to Y while preparing <operation>...') regardless of which of the three called it. findings.title: sell() javadoc (mirroring spec S6) overclaims GriefPrevention always maps overflow in getRemainingClaimBlocks() to 0
findings.scenario: final_spec.json S6 requires: "Javadoc must state this is GriefPrevention's own figure: it includes permission-group bonus blocks and maps arithmetic overflow to 0 (which reads here as blocks-in-use, the safe direction)." The code (line 537-540) reproduces this: "...it maps arithmetic overflow to 0, which reads here as blocks-in-use - the safe direction." javap of PlayerData.getRemainingClaimBlocks() (GriefPrevention-16.18.7.jar) shows TWO distinct try/catch(ArithmeticException) ranges, not one: (1) offsets 0-28 wrap `Math.addExact(accrued, bonus, groupBonus)`; on overflow, the handler at offset 31 does `ldc 2147483647; istore_1` -- clamps to Integer.MAX_VALUE, not 0. (2) offsets 35-75 wrap the per-claim `Math.subtractExact(remaining, claim.getArea())` loop; only THIS overflow is caught at offset 78 and returns `iconst_0`. Concretely: a player whose accrued + bonus + permission-group-bonus sum overflows int range (reachable in a real deployment if `maxPurchasedBlocks` is left at 0/unlimited, since B6's ceiling check is then a no-op and the bonus pool can approach Integer.MAX_VALUE through repeated buys or /adjustbonusclaimblocks) gets `available == Integer.MAX_VALUE` back from S6's `int available = data.getRemainingClaimBlocks();`. The check at line 578 `if (available < blocks) return fail("blocks-in-use", ...)` can then never fire, so a sale of blocks GriefPrevention itself considers committed to claims is silently permitted -- the opposite of the "safe direction" the javadoc promises. Note the spec's own `residual_risks` section already hedges this correctly ("maps arithmetic overflow to Integer.MAX_VALUE or 0 internally"), so this is an internal inconsistency between final_spec.json's S6 instruction and its own residual_risks entry, which the code faithfully inherited without reconciling.
findings.harness_gap: There is no src/test (per CLAUDE.md, none is expected), and nothing in the build cross-checks a javadoc's factual claim about GriefPrevention's bytecode against a javap disassembly of the two distinct overflow branches in PlayerData.getRemainingClaimBlocks(). A harness for this class of finding would javap-diff every bytecode-grounded javadoc sentence against the actual jar, or at minimum construct a PlayerData with accrued+bonus+groupBonus summing past Integer.MAX_VALUE and assert what getRemainingClaimBlocks() returns before trusting the 'safe direction' claim.
findings.fix_hint: Correct the sell() javadoc to state both branches honestly: the accrued+bonus+group-bonus addition overflow clamps to Integer.MAX_VALUE (the unsafe direction -- blocks-in-use cannot fire), while only the per-claim-area subtraction overflow clamps to 0 (the safe direction). If the blocks-in-use refusal must hold even under the addition-overflow path, treat `available == Integer.MAX_VALUE` as suspicious before comparing it to `blocks`, or document the residual risk explicitly rather than asserting a blanket 'safe direction'. The upstream final_spec.json S6 instruction should also be reconciled with its own residual_risks entry so future implementations don't inherit the same overclaim.

missing_injections: CRITICAL: getNameThrows (Player) is built and explicitly earmarked in harness_plan.json ("for the PREPARE row") but no injection in Harness.java ever sets it. This hides a real, reproducible spec violation: in both BarterService.buy() and sell(), the PREPARE try/catch's catch block rebuilds the SEVERE message with a second, unguarded call to player.getName(); if getName() throws persistently (realistic under the same OOM conditions final_spec.json already worries about, since building that message also allocates), the catch handler itself throws and the method propagates an uncaught java.lang.Error instead of logging the SEVERE and returning Result.fail("transaction-failed") that final_spec.json's failure_table row 'B7/S8 PREPARE' requires (operator_sees: 'SEVERE naming the player... nothing moved'). I reproduced this directly with a standalone probe against the harness's own stubs: buy(player,2) with player.getNameThrows=true throws java.lang.Error uncaught with zero log entries recorded, and BarterCommand.java has no try/catch around the buy()/sell() calls to soften this. The 72/72-green harness run gives no signal this exists, even though the exact knob needed to catch it was already built into the Player stub.

throwOnGetStorageContentsCallN (PlayerInventory), described in harness_plan.json as existing 'to make a countCurrency call fail,' is never referenced by any injection (grep count 0). The very first countCurrency(inventory) read at the top of buy() (the 'held < items' check) and the analogous early reads elsewhere are never exercised failing.

returnNullOnDropNumbers (World) and nullStackOnDropNumbers/returnNullStack (Item) are defined in the plan and the stubs but never armed by any injection (grep count 0 each), even though BarterService.deliver() contains defensive checks written for exactly these cases ('entity != null && entity.isValid()' and 'onGround == null ? 0 : onGround.getAmount()'). A regression deleting either null-check (causing an NPE mid-payout) would pass all 72 runs undetected.

lazyLoadThrowsRuntime / lazyLoadThrowsError (PlayerData) are defined but never armed by any injection. warmClaimData()'s first data.getBonusClaimBlocks() call (which triggers the lazy load) is unguarded (no try/catch) in both buy() and sell(); the scenario where that lazy load throws is never exercised, so there is no evidence the resulting uncaught propagation is actually what happens or is acceptable.

throwOnGetClaimsError / throwOnGetClaimsRuntime (PlayerData) are defined but never armed. warmClaimData()'s data.getClaims() call is likewise unguarded; a throwing getClaims() during the warm (central to the whole WARM-DISARMS-SAVE-THREAD design) is never exercised failing.

throwOnGetRemainingError / throwOnGetRemainingRuntime (PlayerData) are defined but never armed. sell()'s unguarded data.getRemainingClaimBlocks() call (used for the blocks-in-use check, before the PREPARE try/catch even starts) throwing is never exercised.

throwOnConstructAfterN / throwOnSetAmountAfterN (ItemStack) are defined in the plan explicitly 'to exercise the deliver allocation-failure row' but neither is ever set by any injection (grep count 0 each). Genuine-heap-exhaustion failure inside deliver()'s per-chunk 'new ItemStack(...)' or inside removeCurrency's 'stack.setAmount(...)' is never exercised, despite final_spec.json's own residual_risks explicitly flagging this class of failure as one the design only 'guarantees... allocation-free in-memory undo and ordering of steps' for, not full recovery -- a claim the harness never actually tests.

Invariant #6 (NO ALLOCATION-BEARING CALL BETWEEN THE TAKE AND THE GRANT) is asserted via checkNoAllocationBetweenTakeAndGrant in exactly one injection, BUY-HAPPY (2 of 72 runs), not in every successful buy despite harness_plan.json listing it under invariants_checked_every_case. BUY-SILENT-WRITE-FAILURE, BUY-LAZY-LOAD-ZERO, WARM-DISARMS-SAVE-THREAD, the boundary 'bought' case in BUY-REFUSE-LIMIT-REACHED, and METADATA-STACKS-NEVER-SPENT all complete a real grant without this check running.

Invariant #7 ORDERING is checked via checkBuyOrdering in only 3 of the buy-success runs and via checkSellOrdering in only 1 sell-success run (SELL-HAPPY), not in every successful trade despite being listed as checked every case. The 'sold' outcome in SELL-PAYOUT-LISTENER-TELEPORTS and the boundary 'sold' outcome in SELL-REFUSE-AMOUNT-TOO-SMALL are never ordering-checked.

Invariant #8's 'exactly one summary record' clause is verified with an explicit countAtLevel(...)==1 check in only 4 of the roughly 30 injections that produce a SEVERE/WARNING (grep confirms exactly 4 call sites: 3 WARNING, 1 SEVERE). Most SEVERE-producing failure injections (BUY-SAVE-OOM-CLEAN-UNWIND, BUY-SAVE-OOM-STALE-WRITER-WINS, BUY-REMOVECURRENCY-THROWS-PARTWAY, BUY-UNDO-OUT-OF-RANGE-GRANT-STANDS, BUY-UNDO-RELATIVE-IN-RANGE, SELL-SAVE-OOM-CLEAN-UNWIND, SELL-UNDO-FAILS-DEDUCTION-STANDS, SELL-UNDO-RELATIVE-IN-RANGE, and every SELL-PAYOUT-* failure case) only confirm a matching SEVERE exists via findAtLevel, never that it is the only one produced; a duplicate or extra spurious log record on any of these paths would slip through undetected.

info()'s claimed guarantee that it 'can never return transaction-failed, items-lost, bought or sold under ANY knob combination' (harness_plan.json's own wording for INFO-WARM-APPLIES-FIX) is checked in exactly one injection with one specific knob (fixNegativeDeficit=50), not swept across INFO-DATASTORE-NULL or any other info()-relevant knob combination; the 'ANY knob combination' claim is asserted in the plan but not actually tested that broadly.

stub_infidelities.real_behaviour: CraftBukkit's addItem mutates the caller's own ItemStack argument in place: the leftover HashMap it returns holds the SAME object the caller passed in, with its amount field reduced to whatever was not placed. This is exactly the behaviour BarterService's own deliver() javadoc asserts and relies on for its reasoning: "The leftover map's values are the argument stacks mutated in place, which is why size was read before the call."
stub_infidelities.stub_behaviour: The stub never mutates the `incoming` argument. It always builds a brand-new ItemStack for the leftover entry (`leftover.put(idx, new ItemStack(incoming.getType(), leftoverAmount, false))`), so the original `stack` object passed into `inventory.addItem(stack)` keeps its original amount (== the chunk size requested) forever, no matter how much was actually placed.
stub_infidelities.impact: No effect on the current 72 passing runs, because BarterService.deliver() only ever reads .getAmount() off the values inside the returned leftover map, never off the original `stack` variable after the call -- so the difference is currently unobservable. But it means this harness cannot detect the exact regression its own javadoc warns about: if deliver() were later 'simplified' to read stack.getAmount() after the addItem() call instead of the pre-captured `size` variable, it would silently miscount on a real Paper server (where that read now returns the leftover, not the requested size) while still passing every injection here (where the stub leaves stack.getAmount() unchanged at `size`).
